newsitem.title: USA: Ten people added to Broin smoke-trail jury pool.
newsitem.headline: Ten people added to Broin smoke-trail jury pool.

text.p: Lawyers questioning potential jurors in the Broin secondhand smoke trial passed 10 people on Tuesday, leaving a jury pool of 93 after nearly four weeks of jury picking.

A telephone company worker, a retired electrical engineer and a house painter were among the people added on Tuesday. The trial judge said he wants a pool of 125 standbys from which six jurors and 10 alternates will be selected.
Dade County Circuit Court Judge Robert Kaye said jury selection would likely go on until after the three-day Fourth of July weekend. Testimony in Norma Broin vs Philip Morris
et al is expected to last two months or longer before a jury will decide whether or not secondhand smoke caused tobacco-related sicknesses among an estimated 60,000 flight attendants.
